panels.rationale: Single-panel image of a Giemsa-stained thin peripheral blood film from a patient with confirmed human African trypanosomiasis due to Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense, showing characteristic trypomastigotes. It is a real patient image with a specific target disease manifestation, with no applicable exclusions. [raw subtype: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense]
panels.attribution_text: Gómez-Junyent et al. Human African Trypanosomiasis in a Spanish traveler returning from Tanzania.. PLoS neglected tropical diseases 2017. doi:10.1371/journal.pntd.0005324. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Trypanosomes in a Giemsa-stained thin blood film from a Spanish traveler returning from Tanzania.
in_text_mentions: The patient was given a follow-up appointment in the OC two days later. She showed persistent fever, but the skin lesion on her neck had enlarged, transforming into a chancre (Fig 1). Cervical lymph nodes were now present on physical examination. HAT due to T. brucei rhodesiense was then suspected. A fine needle aspiration of the chancre was performed, showing flagellate protozoa compatible with trypomastigotes on direct examination. A thin blood film also showed trypomastigotes on Giemsa staining (Fig 2).
